questions.def: Use 'has' with singular subjects in present perfect continuous.
questions.question: She ___ been working here for five years.

questions.def: 'Are going to' expresses a planned future action.
questions.question: They ___ to finish the project by tomorrow.

questions.def: Present perfect 'have done' is used with 'yet'.
questions.question: ___ you ___ your homework yet?

questions.def: 'Would rather' expresses preference.
questions.question: I ___ rather stay home tonight.

questions.def: 'Must' indicates strong probability.
questions.question: He ___ have known about the surprise.

questions.def: 'Is being' creates the present continuous passive voice.
questions.question: He ___ being considered for the promotion.

questions.def: 'Seem to' expresses an appearance or impression.
questions.question: They ___ to have finished the report.

questions.def: 'Had' expresses regret about the past.
questions.question: I wish I ___ studied harder in college.

questions.def: 'Could have' expresses past ability.
questions.question: He ___ ___ spoken French fluently when he was young.

questions.def: 'Would you mind' is a polite request.
questions.question: ___ you mind closing the window?

questions.def: 'Should not have' expresses regret or criticism.
questions.question: You ___ not have eaten so much cake!

questions.def: 'Has been' creates the present perfect passive voice.
questions.question: The decision ___ ___ made by the committee.

questions.def: 'Did tell' emphasizes the action in the past.
questions.question: I ___ told him the truth yesterday.

questions.def: 'Should' expresses expectation or probability.
questions.question: He ___ be arriving any minute now.

questions.def: 'Had had' is the past perfect of 'have to'.
questions.question: He ___ ___ to apologize for his behavior.

questions.def: 'Must have' expresses a logical deduction.
questions.question: They ___ have left already; I saw them go.

questions.def: 'Would rather not' expresses a preference to avoid something.
questions.question: I ___ rather not talk about it now.

questions.def: 'Is being' for a scheduled passive action.
questions.question: She ___ ___ interviewed for the job tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Might be able to' expresses a possibility.
questions.question: I ___ be able to help you later.

questions.def: 'Should have' implies regret or a missed opportunity.
questions.question: You ___ have listened to my advice!

questions.def: 'Did not' is the past simple negative form.
questions.question: He ___ ___ ask for my opinion on the matter.

questions.def: 'Has to' expresses obligation for singular subjects.
questions.question: She ___ to get up early tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Could have' indicates a past possibility.
questions.question: I ___ have gone to the party, but I was tired.

questions.def: Future perfect requires 'will have' + past participle to indicate completion before a time.
questions.question: By the time we arrive, they ___ already left.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous shows duration leading to a future point: 'will have been'.
questions.question: She ___ been working here for five years next month.

questions.def: Past continuous intention uses 'was/were going to' + base form.
questions.question: I ___ going to call you, but I forgot.

questions.def: 'Are supposed to' expresses an obligation or expectation.
questions.question: You ___ to submit the assignment by Friday.

questions.def: 'Was able to' indicates a specific completed action in the past.
questions.question: He ___ finished the report, even though it was difficult.

questions.def: Questions with 'used to' require 'Did' + 'use to' + base form.
questions.question: ___ you ___ (use) to live here?

questions.def: Passive voice past simple uses 'was/were' + past participle.
questions.question: The project ___ completed by the team last week.
